H8035.d: Shem, a son of Noah (often includ. his posterity)

Noah's oldest son. The Semitic peoples, Abraham's line among them, all trace back to him, and Genesis 10 follows his descendants down to Eber.
Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
Son of Joktan, and the ancestor of one of the many Joktanite peoples who settled the Arabian peninsula.

King of Zeboiim, one of the five cities of the plain. He rebelled against Chedorlaomer with the others, and that is what brought the invasion of Genesis 14.

H8004.d: Shalem, an early name of Jerusalem
fb: The old name for Jerusalem. Melchizedek was its king when he came out to bless Abraham, and Psalm 76 uses the name again for the city where God lives.

H8095.d: Shimon, one of Jacob's sons, also the tribe descended from him

Jacob's second son. With his brother Levi he killed the men of Shechem after their sister Dinah was raped. Jacob held it against them on his deathbed.

H8024.d: a Shelanite (collectively), or descendants of Shelah

The clan that came from Shelah, Judah's son by Bath-shua, counted in the census of Numbers 26.

Gilead's son and Manasseh's great-grandson, and his descendants made one of the clans of Manasseh.

H8062.d: a Shemidaite (collectively) or descendants of Shemida

The clan of Shemida, Manasseh's descendant through Gilead, in the Numbers 26 census.

The clan of Shillem, Naphtali's son, in the Numbers 26 census.

H8050.d: Shemuël, the name of three Israelites

Hannah prayed for a son and gave him to the Lord before he was born. He grew up to be the last of the judges and the first great prophet. Israel's first two kings were both anointed by him.

His son Ahihud was picked to help divide Canaan among the tribes. He was an Asherite, and Numbers 34:27 names him for that.

Son of Zophar, among the leading men of Asher in 1 Chronicles 7:37. He is not Shammah son of Agee, David's warrior, though the spellings sit close.

Son of Nahshon and father of Boaz, the same man Ruth and Matthew call Salmon. Chronicles lists him in the line of Judah.
